title: Multi-component dark matter with a populated excited state: electron-recoil lines, low-threshold recoils and the two-state phenomenology across experiments
question: If a fraction f2 of the excited state chi2 survives (metastable or re-populated), what direct-detection signals follow outside LZ's nuclear ROI: the exothermic electron line chi2 e -> chi1 e, light-target nuclear down-scatters, re-population today, and the combined (tau,f2) map?
headline_result: The chi2 e -> chi1 e line at E = delta (Doppler sigma 0.46 keV, S1c 1400-1700 phd, outside LZ's ROI) is 1e6x weaker than the nuclear channel (f2 sigma_e < 3.7e-43 cm2 from an LZ HE-ER estimate); no down-scatter lands below 20 keV on any target; argon gains 21-25x per kg over xenon; halo chi1 chi1 -> chi2 chi2 (v_th = 464 km/s) sustains f2 = 1.3e-5 (m_A'/2.4 GeV)^-8.
key_numbers: T_e = 300 +- 0.53 keV; R_e = 1.12e44 f2 sigma_e /(t yr cm2); nuclear/electron 1.1e6 (300 keV); B_HE = 74 /(t yr keV), S90 = 117; per kg yr per f2: Xe 0.34, Ar 7.1, Si 8.5, Ge 1.6; DEAP-3600 1.5e4 f2 events vs LZ 962; f2_ss = 1.3e-5, crossover m_A' = 2.97 GeV; f2 = 2.8e-3/1e-5 <-> tau = 8.4/4.0e16 s
model_or_mechanism: pseudo-Dirac dark-photon DM (P011) with surviving chi2; exothermic electron and nuclear scattering; halo self-up-scattering steady state
software_and_packages: python 3.12.13; WimPyDD 2.0.4; nestpy 2.1.1; numpy 2.5.3; scipy 1.18.1; pandas 3.0.5; matplotlib 3.11.2; common/lzcommon.py
local_inputs: LZ tex (ROI, Fig.4, Table I), Fig4 PNG, P058/P026/P011/P065/P066 papers, P058 details, P065 script, lzcommon
